app.title: Powergrid Tycoon
scenario.firstRegion.name: The Inherited Grid
scenario.firstRegion.description: You take over an ageing utility. The cheap lignite is in the west, the demand is in the east, and the corridor between them was built for a smaller country.

event.turbineFailure.name: Turbine failure
event.turbineFailure.description: A rotor blade has let go. The unit is out until the parts arrive and the casing is opened.
event.lineFault.name: Transmission fault
event.lineFault.description: Conductors are down across the network. Ratings are cut until the crews have been round.
event.drought.name: Drought
event.drought.description: The rivers are low. There is less water to turn the hydro turbines and less to cool the thermal fleet — one cause, two problems, and they arrive together.
event.severeStorm.name: Severe storm
event.severeStorm.description: A named storm is forecast to cross the region. Expect lines down and turbines shut in.
event.deepFreeze.name: Deep freeze
event.deepFreeze.description: A fortnight of hard frost is coming. Electricity demand rises; heat demand rises further, and heat cannot be shed.
event.fuelPriceSpike.name: Gas price spike
event.fuelPriceSpike.description: Forward gas prices have more than doubled. Everything you burn is about to cost more.
event.interestShock.name: Interest rate shock
event.interestShock.description: Credit has tightened sharply. Everything you build from now on costs more to finance.
event.gasSupplyInterruption.name: Gas supply interruption
event.gasSupplyInterruption.description: Deliveries are being curtailed. Your gas fleet cannot run at anything like full output.
event.coalSupplyDisruption.name: Coal supply disruption
event.coalSupplyDisruption.description: Shipments are held up and the delivered price has jumped.
event.constructionBlockade.name: Construction blockade
event.constructionBlockade.description: Objectors have occupied a site access road. Everything under construction will take longer.
event.choice.prepositionCrews: Pre-position crews and shut in early
event.choice.fillFuelAndHeatStores: Fill the fuel and heat stores
policy.marketLiberal.name: Market liberalisation
policy.marketLiberal.description: Let the market decide. No support for anything, a nominal carbon price, light taxes and quick consents.
policy.renewablesPush.name: Renewables push
policy.renewablesPush.description: A high carbon price, generous tariffs for wind, solar and storage, no new coal, and a harder time consenting anything that burns.
policy.cleanFirm.name: Clean and firm
policy.cleanFirm.description: Long contracts for nuclear, hydro and cogeneration, a capacity market, and fast consents for plant that can be relied on in the hour it is needed.
policy.energySecurity.name: Energy security
policy.energySecurity.description: Domestic fuel first. The carbon price is cut, imports are diversified, consenting is waived — and previous governments' contracts are not honoured.
policy.affordability.name: Consumer prices first
policy.affordability.description: A capped tariff, a levy on revenue earned above a crisis price, and an end to every subsidy consumers were paying for.
policy.fiscalConsolidation.name: Fiscal consolidation
policy.fiscalConsolidation.description: The carbon price stays because it raises money, corporation tax rises, support ends, and a thinner civil service consents more slowly.
